newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Gays beat Church ban, parade in Colombian carnival.
newsitem.headline: Gays beat Church ban, parade in Colombian carnival.

text.p: Gays, transvestites and transsexuals paraded through Colombia's Caribbean port of Barranquilla over the weekend in defiance of a virtual Church ban that threatened to keep them out of an annual carnival.

The 30-day Lenten carnival, one of the biggest in the country, began two weeks ago. But the event organisers, heavily influenced by the city's Archbishop Angel Maria Torres, told homosexuals they could not participate alongside other social groups, the El Espectador newspaper reported.
Faced with loud protests, the organisers lifted the ban late on Saturday.

"We're delighted the ban has been lifted and we will now show Barranquilla that this is about art and culture. We're not at all immoral like the Archbishop is saying," one provocatively dressed transsexual told the NTC TV news programme on Sunday.
Gay carnival-goers will now be allowed to take part in the Grand Parade and the so-called Battle of the Flowers as well as elect their own "Carnival Queen".
